sections.heading: Commodity Jurisdictions (CJs) — DDTC KB0011306
sections.text:
The purpose of a commodity jurisdiction (CJ) request is to determine whether a commodity or service is covered by the U.S. Munitions List (USML) and therefore subject to export controls administered by the U.S. Department of State pursuant to the Arms Export Control Act and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). If after reviewing the USML and other relevant parts of the ITAR, in particular ITAR §120.3, §120.4, and §120.11, you are unsure of the export jurisdiction of a commodity or service, you should request a CJ determination.
Important Notes:
Applicants
Applicants are not required to be registered with DDTC to submit a CJ request.
CJ Requests Are Submitted Electronically
All CJ requests must be submitted via DECCS. Applicants submit CJ requests through an online application using form DS-4076 (to which other documents may be attached). Access the DECCS CJ application. All other submissions will be Returned Without Action.
Returned Without Action (RWA) CJ Requests
In the event you have submitted a CJ request and have received a notice from DDTC indicating it has been RWA’D, we ask that any resubmission include the additional information requested in the RWA notice. We recommend that you include the DDTC RWA letter as an attachment to your new CJ submission. Your resubmission will be processed as a new CJ request and should be submitted accordingly as a new DS-4076.
CJ Case Number
After successful submission of the DS-4076 CJ package through DECCS the applicant receives a CJ case number immediately. If the applicant does not receive a CJ case number, the submission has failed and the applicant must resubmit. Within 48 business hours applicants will be able to track their CJ case in DECCS.

sections.heading: Defense Export Control and Compliance System (DECCS) — DDTC KB0011305
sections.text:
As part of DDTC’s IT Modernization effort, the Defense Export Control and Compliance System (DECCS) will become the central online platform for conducting business with DDTC.
DECCS Industry Portal
DDTC manages several systems to support its core business functions. Read below for more information about each system and the function(s) it supports.
DECCS Applications:
Application
Description
Status
Materials & Guidance
Commodity Jurisdictions (CJ)
The Commodity Jurisdiction (CJ) application was the first application released in DECCS. The CJ application allows industry users to electronically complete, sign and submit a CJ request to determine whether an item or service is covered by the U.S. Munitions List (USML) and therefore subject to export controls administered by the Department of State pursuant to the Arms Export Control Act and the ITAR. Upon successful submission, users will immediately receive their CJ case number for status tracking.

Commodity Jurisdictions (CJs) information
Access the CJ application here.
Opinions (AO)
The Advisory Opinions (AO) application allows industry users to electronically submit inquiries related to ITAR sections 120.22(a), 120.22(c), and 129.9. Use of the application is highly encouraged as a significantly faster alternative to mail-in correspondence, which requires manual data entry and can delay response times.
Live
Please review the following resources related to AOs:
Advisory Opinions (AO) information
Access the DECCS Industry Service Portal here to access the Advisory Opinions application.
Registration
DDTC maintains a pool of approximately 14,000 registered entities, managing renewals, fees, and account data. DDTC replaced its legacy Electronic Form Submission (EFS) tool with the new Registration application. The new application allows industry users to complete the end-to-end registration and renewal processes online, including paying DDTC registration fees using pay.gov.

Licensing
DDTC analyzes and processes approximately 38,000 defense export license applications from industry each year, with input from key interagency partners. DDTC released a new Licensing application to replace its legacy licensing submission system, DTrade. The new application provides the same functionality as DTrade with added data security and convenience.

sections.heading: Advisory Opinions (AOs) & Other Correspondence — DDTC KB0011199
sections.text:
Advisory Opinions
SUBMIT YOUR ADVISORY OPINIONS REQUEST IN DECCS
In order to submit your Advisory Opinions request, click here to access the Advisory Opinions application in DECCS.
DDTC highly encourages submission of Advisory Opinions via DECCS, as this results in the fastest, most direct case processing. Hard copy submission by other means significantly slows down the case processing timeline. If the request cannot be submitted using DECCS, please use the Advisory Opinions form below to ensure all pertinent information is included in the submission.
Advisory Opinions Instructions & Form
Additional Submission Guidance for ITAR Section 120.22(a) Requests
When the request is whether DDTC would be likely to grant a license or other approval for the export of a particular defense article or defense service to a particular country section 120.22(a), DDTC strongly encourages applicants to submit a technical data DSP-5 license application for the marketing of a defense article in lieu of an Advisory Opinions request. Unlike an Advisory Opinion, an approved DSP-5 includes the authorization to export the technical data. The technical data DSP-5 application for the marketing of a defense article must outline in detail the equipment, its proposed usage, the security classification (if any) of the articles or related technical data, and the country or countries involved. Applicants may also include prior related advisory opinions as supporting materials for the application.
About Advisory Opinions
DDTC responds to inquiries on the following topics in the form of Advisory Opinions. Any individual or entity can submit an inquiry. Registration with DDTC is not required to submit an Advisory Opinion.
Preliminary Authorization Determinations
As set forth in ITAR section 120.22(a), a person may request information from the Directorate of Defense Trade Controls as to whether it would likely grant a license or other approval for a particular defense article or defense service to a particular country. Responses are issued on a case-by-case basis and apply only to the particular matters presented, are not binding on the Department of State and may not be used in future matters before the Department. These requests must be made in writing and must outline in detail the equipment, its usage, the security classification (if any) of the articles or related technical data, and the country or countries involved.
Interpretations of the ITAR
As set forth in ITAR section 120.22(c), any person may request an interpretation of the requirements set forth in ITAR. A request for an advisory opinion must be made in writing. Any response to an advisory opinion shall not be an authorization to export and shall not bind the Department to grant or deny any such authorization.
Guidance on Brokering Activities
As set forth in ITAR section 129.9, any person may request in writing guidance as to whether a specific activity constitutes a brokering activity within the scope of part 129. Detailed information regarding the proposed activity must be included in the submission as outlined in section 129.9.
Guidance on Brokering
As set forth in ITAR section 129.9(c), any person desiring guidance on aspects of part 129 other than whether an activity is a brokering activity as described in section 129.9(b) may do so by submitting a description of the relevant facts or copies of relevant documentation.
Inquiries regarding the following topics, and any other topics, will continue to be submitted and responded by mail:
Retransfer/reexport/change in end-use requests (ITAR § 123.9(c))
Related licensing authorizations (ITAR § 120.22(b))
Merger/acquisition notices (ITAR § 122.4)
Dual national/third country national vetting (ITAR § 126.18(a))
Exemption approval requests (ITAR §125.4(b)(11))
SUBMIT OTHER FORMAL INQUIRIES AND CORRESPONDENCE VIA MAIL
To send correspondence to DDTC, please mail in your correspondence to:
U.S. Department of State
Directorate of Defense Trade Controls
Compliance & Registration Division
2401 E Street NW, SA-1 Room H1200
Washington, DC 20037
Note: Please refer to the ITAR sections referenced above for details on the information that should be included in your correspondence.
